item.title: Uyghur
item.description:
Uyghur phrases which show the grammatical breakdown of the language.

This is inspired by the work of Tim Ferriss and his advice for learning languages affectively.

It is important to note that the Uyghur language follows the Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) word order, which is different from the Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) word order in English.

The apple is red. Alma qizil.

It is John’s apple. U John’ning almisi.

I give John the apple. Men John’ge alma barimen.

We give him the apple. Biz uning’gha alma berimiz.

He gives it to John. U uni John’ge beridu.

She gives it to him. U uni uning’gha beridu.

item.title: Caution and Creativity
item.description:
I recently received a LinkedIn suggested prompt that got me thinking: | You’re juggling creativity and caution in your project. How can you avoid potential pitfalls?

From a software perspective, it is important to not migrate to the flashiest tools or technologies solely because they are modern or popular.

Use the right tool for the job, maintain good client expectations, and, as always, keep your people happy. Creativity will naturally find its way in!

I think this is a very simple way to view things; there’s already too much complexity in software. Keep it simple.
